To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) trustful and trustworthy behaviors can be driven by different motives and (2) the second player’s choices in the TG can be used to disentangle the motives underlying trustors’ choices.

(1) trustors and trustees have different motives, (2) there is a non-trivial proportion of individuals who act out of (self-interested) strategic motives when they trust, (3) these individuals are not trustworthy as they do not reciprocate trust, and (4) there are individuals who act out efficiency motives when they trust and who are trustworthy.
(1) the motives underlying trustful behaviors differ substantially, and (2) trustworthiness can be used to identify the motives of trustful individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that motives play in the trust game.
the heterogeneity of motives underlying trustful and trustworthy behaviors.
the heterogeneity of motives in the TG and the implications of this heterogeneity for our understanding of trust.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are at least two different types of trustful behavior, and that the second player’s decision can provide important information to disentangle the two.
trustful and trustworthy behaviors are driven by different motives.
there is no single factor that determines trustful and trustworthy behaviors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of the trustee is key to understanding the role of motives in trust.
there are two distinct types of people who trust others in a TG: those who do it out of self-interest and those who do it for social reasons.
trustful and trustworthy behaviors can be motivated by different social motives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two types of trustful individuals: those that act out of social preferences, and those who are strategic.
the dual-role TG is a useful tool in studying heterogeneous motives of trustful and trustworthy behaviors.
there is no one-size-fits-all explanation of trustful or trustworthy behavior in the TG, but instead a variety of different social motives are at play.
